page_title: Requestly: Design, Build and Test APIs

summary.name: Requestly
summary.one_liner: Requestly is a Git-native API client and API platform for designing, testing and managing REST and GraphQL APIs, available as a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux.
use_cases: Testing REST and GraphQL endpoints during development
Storing API collections in a Git repository for version control and code review
Switching API environments between local, staging and production
Writing scripted API tests with assertions
Sharing API collections with a team in a shared workspace
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Requestly as a lightweight desktop API client for macOS, Windows and Linux that stores collections as local files that can be kept in Git. It supports organizing requests into collections, switching environments and variables (global, collection and environment scopes), and sending requests with params, headers, body and auth. Pre-request and post-response JavaScript scripts can set variables, chain auth and assert on response data, and a collection runner is included. It can import collections from Postman, cURL and OpenAPI, and offers GraphQL support with schema introspection. The site also mentions local, team sync and self-hosted data options, plus SOC-2 compliance, SSO, role-based access control and audit logs for enterprise use.
notable: Git-native: API collections stored as plain JSON files on your machine and synced via Git
Imports Postman, cURL and OpenAPI collections, including collections, environments and auth
Local, team sync or self-hosted data options; secrets kept local
Enterprise features: SOC-2 compliance, SSO, role-based access control and audit logs
caveats: Pricing is described only as 'flat per-user pricing' with no amounts given on the page
Enterprise security and team features are positioned for paid business use; specific plan details are not listed on the page
Page is largely marketing; the platform list comes from the download section and may not include every system
